title: Signal and Observable Performance knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Signal and Observable Performance”?
options: Signal and Observable Performance means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Signal and Observable Performance removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Signal and Observable Performance should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Signal and Observable Performance helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Signal and Observable Performance helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Signal and Observable Performance is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Fine-grained reactive updates” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Fine-grained reactive updates” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Fine-grained reactive updates” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Fine-grained reactive updates” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Fine-grained reactive updates” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Fine-grained reactive updates” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Fine-grained reactive updates” under Signal and Observable Performance. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Signal and Observable Performance”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
